Irrigate where possible.
Flushing of trees will occur since this normally occurs due to the rains.
If rains last for two or more days, fungal and bacteria can become an issue.
Pests concentrate heavily on the few flushing trees. Mites build fast in hot/dry weather; Drunken Baymen may still be attracted to new flush/soft growth.
Psyllids reproduce on new leaf flushes.
Rains favor the proliferation of fungi and spread of nematodes
Could be critical if plants are affected in the Reproductive Stage.
Crop can be planted earlier than normal.
Low plant density is recommended and have adecuate drainge.
Borer symptoms (soursop): frass (sawdust), holes, gumming, wilting branches, sudden dieback.
Cacao disease risk rises when canopy stays wet and airflow is poor—black pod spreads faster when sanitation is weak and pods remain on the ground/tree.
Dust + heat favours mites/thrips; flush growth after showers favours aphids/mealybugs/scale.
Even under “No concern,” 80–160 mm can be uneven (short dry spells between showers). Most problems appear in edge rows, shallow soils, young plantings, and unmulched blocks.
Mealybugs/scales are flagged by ants, honeydew and sooty mold—ants protect them and make control harder.
Mites build rapidly in hot/dry weather: look for stippling/bronzing, leaf curl and fine webbing (where present).
Thrips damage shows as bronze/scabby scars on young avocado fruit and distorted tender leaves.
Under drought watch, pests concentrate on the few trees/areas that still flush (near irrigation lines, moist spots). When showers come, flush bursts happen and sucking pests rebound fast.
Watch early drought symptoms: midday wilting, leaf scorch, premature fruit drop, smaller fruit, sunburn patches.

Watch early warning signs: leaf bronzing/stippling, curled young leaves, sticky honeydew/sooty mold (scale/mealybugs), borer frass at trunks/branches, premature fruit drop, fruit scarring, and sunburn patches.
An increase in temperature accelerates evaporation, lowering pond water levels and reducing the flow of the New River, which may become stagnant and lead to a deterioration in water quality.

An increase in temperature elevates physiological and metabolic activity, leading to greater overall activity and higher oxygen consumption, which reduces dissolved oxygen (DO) concentrations in the water.
Elevated temperatures may promote a shift from beneficial bacterial communities to pathogen-dominated conditions, thereby increasing susceptibility to disease.
Increase in temperature cause evaporation affecting pond water levels and increasing salinity
Rising temperatures lead to higher shrimp feed intake, which may degrade water quality as uneaten feed accumulates and decomposes.
